h: Stanley Park and the Rest of Inland Blackpool
p: Here's the clever bit about Blackpool Zoo: it sits beside Stanley Park, a cracking big town park, and most visitors never think to explore it. Laid out in the 1920s, the park has a big boating lake, formal Italian Gardens with a fountain, wide avenues of trees and a handsome Art Deco café. It's a calm, green contrast to the noise and neon of the Golden Mile.

Also within the park, Blackpool Model Village and Gardens has detailed miniature scenes set among landscaped gardens, a gentle, quirky stop that works for small children and grandparents alike. Put it together with the zoo and you've got a full day without ever smelling a doughnut stall, which is quite an achievement in Blackpool.

Timing is everything here. School holidays and sunny weekends get busy, so arriving close to opening gives you the animals before the crowds. In autumn, the Illuminations season brings huge numbers of visitors into town, which means the zoo can make a great daytime plan before an evening drive or tram ride along the lights.

Getting there is easy by car, with the zoo signposted off the M55 as you come into Blackpool, and buses link it with the town centre. If you're staying on the front, a taxi is quick and saves fiddling with parking. Don't forget sun cream on bright days; there's a lot of open ground.
